| [NOTE-310](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-310.md) | Notes on Landauer's principle, reversible computation, and Maxwell's Demon | Bennett states Landauer's principle as a consequence of the Second Law. | [NOTE-417](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-417.md) | Nonequilibrium Equality for Free Energy Differences | The nonequilibrium work relation. Switch a classical system that starts in canonical equilibrium from H_0 to H_1 at any finite rate. Then ⟨e^{−βW}⟩ = e^{−βΔF} exactly, whatever the path or the switching time (Eq. 2). It is proved for an isolated Hamiltonian system by Liouville's theorem, for a reservoir under weak coupling, and for a Nosé–Hoover thermostat with no extra assumption. | [NOTE-420](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-420.md) | Stochastic thermodynamics, fluctuation theorems and molecular machines | The 2012 reference review of stochastic thermodynamics. | [NOTE-709](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-709.md) | Ostwald — Studies on the formation and transformation of solids, I | Ostwald times how small a crystal fragment can be and still seed a supercooled melt or supersaturated solution (down to about 10⁻⁹–10⁻¹² g). He shows that only the solid substance itself, or a strictly isomorphous solid, seeds. He divides states beyond equilibrium into metastable ones, which change only on contact with the other phase, and labile ones, where the new phase forms spontaneously. In §§32–41 he states the rule later called the rule of stages: on leaving a state, the form reached is "not the most stable ... but the nearest" (pp. 306–307), meaning the form with the next-highest free energy. He offers it "not as a law" but as "a frequently applicable rule" (p. 308), drawn from experience and backed by an analogy with the van der Waals isotherm. The rule covers spontaneous formation only. Whether a metastable intermediate goes on to the next form depends on whether it is labile with respect to it; if it is merely metastable it stays until seeded (p. 308). The word "Stufenregel" does not appear in the paper. | Read |
